scenarioStory.history: 79-year-old female stood up from the breakfast table, reported feeling suddenly dizzy and lightheaded, and briefly lost consciousness. Husband caught her partially before she slid to the kitchen floor. She regained consciousness within approximately 20 seconds without any postictal confusion. She now complains of persistent dizziness, weakness, and mild nausea; denies chest pain, denies head strike, denies tongue biting or incontinence.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 79-year-old female seated in a kitchen chair, pale and diaphoretic, alert but reporting dizziness and weakness following a brief syncopal episode. Radial pulse is slow and regular. 12-lead EKG is indicated given her age, cardiac history risk factors, and syncope presentation. → Instability recognized: 12-lead confirms complete (third-degree) AV block with a ventricular escape rate of 32. Blood pressure has dropped further and the patient is becoming more fatigued with recurrent lightheadedness, consistent with ongoing hemodynamic instability. → Atropine ineffective: Atropine produces no meaningful change in heart rate or blood pressure, as expected with third-degree AV block. The crew moves directly to transcutaneous pacing with appropriate sedation/analgesia. → Paced and stabilized: Transcutaneous pacing achieves reliable electrical and mechanical capture at a rate of 70. Perfusion and mentation improve. Patient is prepared for transport with continuous monitoring.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 79-year-old female seated in a kitchen chair, pale and diaphoretic, alert but reporting dizziness and weakness following a brief syncopal episode. Radial pulse is slow and regular. 12-lead EKG is indicated given her age, cardiac history risk factors, and syncope presentation.
relatedChecklist: Manage airway as necessary; position patient of comfort
Initiate cardiac monitoring and acquire 12-lead EKG
Screen geriatric fall patient for occult trauma from the fall

scenarioEvents.name: Instability recognized
scenarioEvents.description: 12-lead confirms complete (third-degree) AV block with a ventricular escape rate of 32. Blood pressure has dropped further and the patient is becoming more fatigued with recurrent lightheadedness, consistent with ongoing hemodynamic instability.
relatedChecklist: Recognize symptomatic bradycardia with hemodynamic instability (HR 32, BP 78/50, recurrent near-syncope)
Atropine 1 mg IV push (fixed dose; may repeat q3-5 min, max total 3 mg)
Reassess vital signs closely following atropine administration

scenarioEvents.name: Atropine ineffective
scenarioEvents.description: Atropine produces no meaningful change in heart rate or blood pressure, as expected with third-degree AV block. The crew moves directly to transcutaneous pacing with appropriate sedation/analgesia.
relatedChecklist: Recognize third-degree block unlikely to respond to atropine; proceed to TCP without delay
Provide sedation/analgesia with pacing for patient comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Paced and stabilized
scenarioEvents.description: Transcutaneous pacing achieves reliable electrical and mechanical capture at a rate of 70. Perfusion and mentation improve. Patient is prepared for transport with continuous monitoring.
relatedChecklist: Confirm mechanical and electrical capture; titrate pacer output/rate for adequate perfusion
Reassess vital signs and mental status after capture achieved
Transport with continuous cardiac monitoring for further evaluation

scenarioEvents.name: Pacing delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Transcutaneous pacing is delayed after atropine fails, allowing the patient to continue decompensating. Heart rate and blood pressure fall further, and mental status deteriorates toward unresponsiveness.
relatedChecklist: Recognize impending hemodynamic collapse; proceed directly to TCP without further delay
Recognize decreasing level of consciousness and worsening shock as signs of critical hypoperfusion
